evals.prompt: Here is a front and side turnaround of a knight character (ref/knight_front.png, ref/knight_side.png). Build him in Blender as a game-ready character for a third-person action game in Unity, about 1.85 m tall, rigged, with LOD0 to LOD2. Don't ask me questions unless you really have to.
evals.expected_output: asset-brief.md with measured proportions; CH_Knight master with calibration; blockout and forms compare sheets with IoU numbers from the reference camera; LOW meshes passing validate.py within budget; baked textures; DEF rig with hand sockets; GLB per LOD with asset-manifest.json; roundtrip report; final report listing inferred parts

evals.prompt: Recreate this dune buggy from the concept (ref/buggy_concept.jpg) as a drivable vehicle asset for Godot. Separate wheels with proper pivots, doors that open, a collision hull, GLB export.
evals.expected_output: vehicle brief with wheelbase, track, wheel diameter and clearance estimated from cues; lofted body shell; wheels as separate objects with origins at the axle; hinge pivots on doors; COL_ hull; sockets for seats and exhaust; steering-lock and suspension pose sheet; manifest listing inferred underside

evals.prompt: I have a photo of a stone chapel (ref/chapel.jpg). I need a modular kit I can snap together on a 2 m grid in three.js: walls, window wall, doorway, corner, pillar, arch, roof segment, plus the door as a separate hinged object. Tileable materials with a trim sheet.
evals.expected_output: architecture brief with storey height, opening rhythm and wall thickness from door and step cues; kit pieces with origins at grid corners and shared thickness constants; 2x2 assembly render with no seams; door pivot at the hinge; simple colliders; tileable UV scale checked against the ruler; GLB kit with manifest

evals.prompt: Attached are a character model sheet (ref/ranger_sheet.png: front, side and back views plus face and belt detail panels in one image) and a separate painted three-quarter concept (ref/ranger_concept.jpg). Build her in Blender as a game-ready hero character for Unreal, about 1.70 m tall, rigged, with LOD0 and LOD1.
evals.expected_output: asset-brief.md listing each panel of the sheet with its pixel box, scale and ground line; the front, side and back panels cropped into separate reference files that share one scale; the three-quarter concept used for silhouette and surface detail only, never proportions; world-registered gate IoU per orthographic view on cleaned mattes; conflicts between the sheet's views recorded as deviations; rigged GLB per LOD with a manifest listing inferred parts

evals.prompt: The knight you built passes the gates, but up close the face looks low-poly and uncanny, the ears look folded, the hands are blocky and don't really hold the sword, the boots look like slabs, the knee plates are domes, a buckle and the pouches float off the belt, and the sword clips through his leg in some poses. Make him look realistic; I care more about that than the 35k cap.
evals.expected_output: close-up renders from fixed cameras before and after; head, hands and feet rebuilt on CC0 anatomical base meshes fitted to the blueprint (landmark fit, real eyes and ears) with the source and licence in the manifest; boots on a realistic last with the painted-length deviation recorded; shaped knee and elbow cops on half-bend helper bones; validate.py --attachments from the brief's attaches-to column with no floating parts; hand sockets seated in the open hand and fingers closed on the weapon mesh in every pose; the idle stance from the concept on the extreme-pose sheet; pose_overlap.py with no weapon pairs except the glove on its grip; the budget tier moved with the reason recorded; a before/after sheet in the report

evals.prompt: Second look at the knight in the viewer. The sword in his right hand still doesn't look gripped: the fingers are curled and smashed against the handle, not wrapped round it. The shield hand has the palm facing the wrong way. In the bind pose the sheathed sword is off centre and clips through the scabbard. The cape clips through the shoulder plates, its back floats below the cowl instead of joining it, the brooch floats on the breastplate, and I can see a ghost ear in the face texture and nostrils on the side of the nose.
evals.expected_output: per-segment gap measurements for both hands before and after (palm and every phalanx within about 6 mm of the handle), from a grip seat at the base of the fingers and a wrap search over the knuckle and middle joints; the centre-grip shield held as a punch into the boss with the boss deep enough for the closed fist, fingers tested against thin shells; the sheathed weapon attached at the hip socket in the bind pose with the hilt centred on the blade, the scabbard's mouth below the guard behind a slotted throat, hangers riveted on the belt and landing on the side facing it, and zero intersections at rest; the simulated cowl smoothed and cleared with steel and soft gaps, lying over the cloak's top as the concept shows, the cloak tucked under one pauldron and over the other with no cloak-pauldron pairs; the brooch seated on the cowl; texture fixes for the duplicated ear and side nostrils; before/after viewer captures from the same cameras

evals.prompt: Third pass on the armoured character. The shoulder plates still clip at the bottom, and the left one looks taller than the right: make both like the right. The cape's top at the back needs a better shape and flow: I can see armour between the cape and the hood. Shouldn't the brooch join the cloak to the breastplate? The leg armour doesn't fit at the back of the legs, the skin behind the ear is a smudge, and there are dark spots on the side of the nose. The idle grip on the held item still looks wrong; I've put some Mixamo clips in ref/anim you can use for poses.
evals.expected_output: layered shoulder plates built inside out (lowest lame over the sleeve, the cap last), each lame a straight band hugging the layer beneath, trims seated on the fitted plates, and zero cap, lame and sleeve intersections at rest, with both sides built from one definition mirrored about each shoulder joint and the deviation from the concept recorded; the cloak raised along the shoulder line under a hood-like collar whose sides pass over the cloak's top edge, zero cloak-collar intersections; the collar drawn onto the breastplate at the brooch; the garment layer order at the legs checked from behind (trousers into boots, plates over them, straps over the plates); painted ear and nostril remnants repainted from donor regions with a feathered mask; the idle arm taken from a reference clip so the hand keeps a near-neutral roll, with no new intersection in the idle; LODs built from the finished high-detail cloth; before/after viewer captures from the same cameras

evals.prompt: The test poses in the viewer look cartoonish: arms thrown straight up, a stiff crouch, a stride that just swings the legs. Either remove them or fix them properly using the Mixamo clips I put in asset-lib/mixamo. Also the brooch floats in front of the chest plate when it should touch it.
evals.expected_output: each test pose replaced by a real frame from a reference clip that loads the same joints, retargeted with rest frames aligned on two anatomical axes (the palm's normal for the hands), limbs rolled into their hinge planes, no bending past rest, the forearm's roll at the wrist, the root scaled and the lower sole grounded; held props aimed at the clip's prop placement instead of copying a hand that holds a different kind of prop, each candidate scored with an exact mesh intersection test against the posed body as well as sampled clearance; bone-chain cloth hung under gravity against capsule proxies of the body and of the gear hung on it (scabbard, straps); poses named after what each sampled frame shows in a render of the clip, not the clip's title; weapon claims read back from the overlap report pose by pose; posed intersection counts before and after, with the remaining deformation limits recorded; the fastener squared to the plate under its whole footprint and resting on the cloth and plate with the cloth laid flat under it, checked with a section; before/after viewer captures

evals.prompt: In some poses, especially 2 and 5, the shoulder armor is extremely bent and appears crushed as if there isn't even anything inside of the armor. That does not appear realistic at all, please fix.
evals.expected_output: diagnosis that the plates share the padding's blended clavicle-to-arm weights, so linear blend skinning bends the rigid shell; the pauldron made one rigid shell on a helper bone (clavicle parent, the upper arm's rest orientation, Copy Rotation of a fraction of the upper arm's turn) with the pivot and fraction chosen by measured contacts across every test pose, per-plate helpers rejected when the plates are not built to slide; the sleeve under the plates riding the helper and handing over to the arm in the bare gap between the lowest lame and the elbow plate, with an edge loop added at each end of that gap on the delivery meshes only (the simulation colliders and fitting layers unchanged); no new contact in the idle; the cloak lifted by the raised pauldron; the runtime helper rule in the manifest using the rest rotations; before/after close-ups of both shoulders in the named poses and intersection counts
